[h1]A classic game made timeless by developer and player support[/h1]
[h3]2024 Edit:[/h3] With the introduction of Steam Workshop integration and a completely unexpected 2023 patch that enabled 64-bit support, Empire at War is in its best state ever.

[h3]Original 2014 Review:[/h3] Plenty of bang for your buck, with three campaigns, about a dozen turn-based conquest modes, and classic skirmish battles. However, if you're an experienced RTS fan, you might find the ground battles lacking. The unit controls are imprecise, the balance questionable, and the pop limit placed painfully low. 

That said, the space battles are magnificent. Each class of ship has its place, and the pop limit gives you far more breathing room. The game just shines here.

And when vanilla bores you, check out some of the mods on moddb. I personally recommend the Revenge of Thrawn and Republic at War projects, both of which introduce a plethora of new units familiar to longtime Star Wars fans.

Star Wars Empire at War and it's expansion Forces of Corruption (included in the Gold Pack) are a must buy for a Star Wars fan looking for a worthy RTS to soak some hours into.
I may not have many hours on my Steam copy, but I assure you I played this all the time on my old PC back when it came out. You could say it was my childhood pc game.
In this game you can play a story campaign of all 3 factions: Empire, Rebellion and the Zann Consortium. The Empire and Rebellion ones take place before and during A New Hope. (You need to run the Empire at War Gold Edtion game to play this) The Consortium campaign takes place after this. (You need to run the Forces of Corruption game to play this) I'm putting this behind it as it's a bit unclear to newer players.

But the game really shines in the next part of the game: Galactic Conquest. This is where you will put most of your hours in. A real-time sandbox campaign with the goal to take over the Star Wars Galaxy. You can do this with the 3 factions listed above. As the Empire you can build the Super Star Destroyer: Executor and the best of all... the Death Star! (Death Star I in EaW and Death Star II in FoC) I really enjoy playing as the Empire with all its technical marvels. But beware even your greatest piece of technological terror has a weakness... and others are desperate to exploit it!
But the conquest works as follows: you have an X amount of starting systems, which you can upgrade with bigger space stations and build bases on to increase income, your army or build it into an impenatrable fortress. To capture a planet one must first destroy the fleet and station in orbit, then you must prepare your troops for a ground assault. After winning both battles the planet is yours! I would get this game for this sandbox experience alone. 

And then there's Skirmish, the mode where you can play on a vast selection of space and ground maps with all the units available in the Galactic Conquest mode (except the big ones like the Executor and Death Stars). Here you start with a space station (in space) or a ground base with pre-built buildings and defences which you can upgrade (on the ground). The focus here is more on epic battles than on base building, you can still put down turrets, repair and healing stations. 
I played this less, but it's still good fun. 

And then you have multiplayer! Yes! Since a few months ago, Disney gave the all-clear to the developers from back in 2006 to release new updates to the game! In the first patch they added Multiplayer which was gone for quite some time after GameSpy got shut down, it's now integrated into Steam! Furthermore they fixed bugs and crashes that were still present in the game. And best of all they made installing mods quicker and easier with the addition of the Steam Workshop! 

And then we come to the final part of this review.. the mods! The mods for this game are amazing, from mods that add new units and maps to enormous overhauls that change the setting from Galactic Civil War to the Clone Wars era! This means that when the base game starts getting old, you can just download a nice mod from the Workshop or Moddb and get a whole new experience! 
I played tons of Republic at War, Phoenix Rising with my CD copy. Now I found new ones like Battlefront Commander and Awakening of the Rebellion. 

So should you get this game? Well I think you know the answer by now. The game is very stable, yes some crashes here and there but thats mostly when playing mods. The game has plenty of content worth of 100s of hours. Great community and modding community with amazing mods. 
I'm grateful to the devs for making this game. If you are a Star Wars fan and like strategy and RTS? Yes get it now! As Darth Vader said many times: "It is your destiny..."

Also, a few sentences that will describe the experience of playing this game:
- We will crush this Rebellion with one swift stroke!
- Everything that has transpired has done so according to my design....
- General, prepare your troops for a surface attack!
- Lord Vader, you may start your landing. The shield will be down in moments.
- It's a TRAP!
- Intensify forward firepower! IT'S TOO LATE! *explodes*
- They came from behind! *explodes*
Most games have you take the POV of the Rebellion so it's a nice change to play as the Empire and crush the Rebel scum

I have (at the time of writing) played this game for 61.2 hours and I can safely say that it is a brilliant game. Over the course of playing, I have played using two different mods as well as the base game. On all of my playthroughs I have enjoyed playing the game, particularly during...

-+-SPACE COMBAT-+-

The Space Combat is a standard RTS, but with several added features. The most important of these features is Hardpoints. Instead of attacking a target with it at full power until the moment it breaks up, you target specific systems, such a Tractor Beams (to prevent the enemies from trapping ships) or Hangar Bays, to stop them from releasing fighters. The next is Unit Abilities. These allow you to perform special actions to give yourself the upper hand in combat. An example of this is the Acclamators's Weapon Boost (Which is shared with most Imperial units). Overall, I really enjoy it.

-+-GROUND COMBAT-+-
I must admit, I do not enjoy the [i]base game[/i] ground combat because there are too few units and it is visually uninteresting (Though I do cut some slack for it being a very old game). Mods, however, greatly improve it, adding better maps and more units. If you are going to be spending alot of time on the ground, I recommend the Cone Wars mod, which makes each unit moveable on it's own, instead of in groups. 

-+-MODS-+-
Start by playing the base game, then ook into mods. Most mods are complete conversions and rely on you knowing the basics of the game. I recommend Clone Wars and Thrawn's Revengem the latter is receiving an update soon and the prior is complete.

-+-VERDICT-+-
STAR WARS: Empire at War is a brilliant game, and I recommend it even if you don't like Star Wars (There are mods that change the setting)

A great game that today is largely kept alive by a highly dedicated modding community, with several outstanding mods available, though the base game still holds up well on its own. At the time of release, this was one of the if not the most innovative RTS titles, and it does an excellent job of honoring its source material in terms of quality and presentation. My actual playtime is probably well over 600 hours. I originally owned the boxed version of both the base game and its expansion and only purchased the Steam edition after my discs were damaged. The game offers three distinct RTS gameplay layers that blend together seamlessly, all of which are further expanded in the Forces of Corruption expansion. There is a galaxy map mode where you manage planets, direct armies, and handle strategic decisions. Combat is split into two parts space battles and ground engagements. Space combat allows you to command fleets, target enemy ships or specific subsystems, and micromanage encounters to gain an advantage. Ground combat is more traditional RTS fare, with squads of infantry and vehicles under your command. Notably, you don’t construct buildings during battles beyond a few limited defensive structures placed in specific locations combat relies entirely on the units you bring in from the galaxy map.

Visually, the game is still impressive for its age, especially the space battles. Destroyed ships breaking apart, burning, and exploding remain satisfying to watch even by today’s standards. The musical score fits the setting well, though it could benefit from a few more original tracks. The main drawbacks are minor compatibility issues on newer versions of Windows, which can occasionally lead to crashes, and some awkward unit pathfinding particularly in space combat. At times, getting ships to move exactly where you want requires extra micromanagement and careful clicking. Overall, this is an excellent RTS that I can confidently recommend, even at full price. If you’re interested primarily because of the popular mods, I strongly suggest playing the base game first. While a bit clunky due to its age, it provides essential knowledge and context. Many mods are more complex, more difficult, and lack tutorials, as they assume a solid understanding of the core game mechanics.

A MUST FOR STAR WARS FANS.

It's one of the highest rated games of all time on Steam, and rightfully so. Even over a decade later, I still get the urge to play this game from time to time. 

I'll start with the original game, Empire at War. Though it's a great game on its own, the expansion pack absolutely takes it to the next level, and I'll go over that later. There is a campaign for both the Rebellion and the Empire, of which only the Rebellion campaign used to be canon in Legends. The Empire campaign, on the other hand, offers an alternate ending for Star Wars. These campaigns are excellent, and overall they really make you feel like you are commanding a small section of the Rebellion or Empire as you expand and eventually unlock the entire galaxy to conquer. They are somewhat short by 2022 standards, and do conflict with some of the new canon, but they are still a blast to play. 

Going into said conquering mechanics, battles are fought in two theaters; on land, and in space. Of the two, space combat is by far the most enjoyable. I love space combat in this game. Even today, the gameplay still holds up. There is something so addicting to these space battles that makes players such as myself come back for more and more. The scale of some of these battles are simply jaw dropping. There has not been, and probably never will be, another Star Wars experience like it. 

On the other land, land combat is more hit or miss. Though it still can be very fun, it is a bit slow for my liking. I found myself enjoying the campaign land battles a good bit, but when I play the other modes, I tend to auto-resolve the land battles unless I’m defending against a large force and I know I’ll lose if I auto-resolve. I’d rather spend my time in space combat, but land battles still can be very exciting from time to time. 

Speaking of the other modes, there is a sort of Instant Action mode where you can fight a single battle on or above any planet of your choosing, and then the fabled Galactic Conquest. It’s almost a sort of mythical game concept these days, since EA has outright and blatantly refused to recreate anything like it. Essentially, you play as either the Rebels or the Empire, with the Black Sun Pirates being a stationary roadblock on some planets to slow the expansion of either side. You build up a space fleet and start destroying the enemy’s space stations to clear the way for a ground force to actually conquer the planet. If you choose the Empire, you can build the Death Star and simply reduce heavily-defended fortress planets to asteroids. Because there are only two players, you and the AI’s faction, the mode in the base game gets old relatively quickly. 
The game uses the phenomenal, classic music from the Star Wars movies. The graphics for space combat still hold up relatively well today, though land combat and cutscenes do look more dated.

The expansion pack is Forces of Corruption. Some people think of this pack as two games in one; it is not. Force of Corruption doesn’t add new campaigns for Rebels or the Empire, in fact you can’t even access them in Forces of Corruption. It does however add new units for them, for use in Galactic Conquest and the instant action mode. The crown jewel of Forces of Corruption is the Zann Consortium, a new playable faction. It is a group of pirates, smugglers, and other criminals led by the mastermind of crime Tyber Zann. This is unlike anything seen in a Star Wars game, before or since. The criminal underworld is criminally underexplored in Star Wars canon and this game offers an incredible look into it. 

There is a campaign for the Zann Consortium, and it is an absolute must-experience for any Star Wars fan. There is one very specific character in the campaign that has become very popular because of rumors of him appearing in the Ashoka show. It’s absolutely fantastic to see him in a Star Wars game, because his appearances since then have been few and far between. I do have a few problems with it that keep me from ranking it as my favorite game of all time though. 

The game is somewhat buggy, and the auto-save feature has been disabled on the Steam version, at least for Windows 11. I’ve had key heroes disappear right before I needed to send them to a specific planet for a mission, and there was no way of getting them back other than starting a new game. Additionally, I’ve had some space battle glitches where proton torpedo launchers start firing constantly, like a machine gun, and I had some problems with the Zann Consortium space station special weapon ability. 

The campaign is also incredibly short. Even by 2006 standards, this is a really, really short campaign. It only took me about three hours to finish it from start to end, not counting the times I had to restart due to bugs and glitches. There are fully fleshed out hero units in the campaign that are barely even used, and at least three specific ground units that come too late to actually do anything, as the remaining missions by that point are stealth missions and space battles. It definitely feels like they cut several missions from the campaign towards the end. 

Nevertheless, this is an absolutely outstanding game, partly because of the modding community. That’s right! Even over a decade later, this game still has a huge and very active modding community. These mods are often total overhaul mods, improving every single aspect of the game. My favorite is Republic at War, which places the game in the Clone Wars era. 

If you like Star Wars, get this game. If you like strategy games, get this game. If you like any sort of space battles, get this game. Heck, even if you never played a strategy game before, get this game. It is, in my opinion, an absolute must have for anyone who even remotely likes anything this game touches upon. The only thing that really disappointed me about this game is that we will never see anything like it ever again.

Short answer: Yes

Public service announcement: If you find that the game suddenly doesn't launch from Steam anymore, closing after a second or two without any warnings or error messages whatsoever, try setting all six executables to compatibility mode for WinXP SP3 and Run as Admin. These are the StarWarsG.exes, the sweaw and swfoc.exes and the runme/runme2.exes in the root folder. Then make sure that the Steam.exe is Run as Admin as well - it will complain about being in compatibility mode but ignore it. I don't know how or why the game spontaneously stopped working - I had un/reinstalled everything, including C++ redists, cleared the registry, you name it. Only the above got it to work.

In conclusion, the game is pretty much fun and I would suggest to buy this in 2021, or any other future years because this game is pretty fun when it comes to Forces Of Corruption, Mods, and many more other things that are supported in this game. I have been playing this game since 2008, first on Disk which had countless hours, and now through steam. No matter what I always come back to this RTS, but I do so because the modding community has pushed the limits of this game beyond its initial intention giving it a crazy long life span, and a dedicated fan base. Recommend playing the base game through the campaigns to get you familiar but mods are really where this game shines.

Recommendations for mods:
EAWX: Thrawns Revenge, Fall of the Republic, and Revans Revenge
Awakening of the Rebellion
Awakening of the Clone Wars
